Header: Digitaria abyssinica East Africa: lumbugu, sangari; Ethiopia: bora, sargida, sari-zaba, ura, waria, wariote; Kenya: blue couch, chemorut, ekenyambi, lumbugu sogule, ombugo, siratet, thangari; Tanzania: sanguri

Prevention: Purchase certified crop seed and animal feed to reduce the chance of contamination
As seeds can travel on animals and machinery, do not allow animals into an affected area, limit machinery use in the area and keep machinery clean to prevent spread
Keep crop healthy to maximize competitiveness - use optimal water and fertilizer levels
Monitoring: Creeping, perennial grass, rhizomatous; 50-100 cm high
Leaves: flat; bluish-green 15 cm long, 2-8 mm wide
Rhizomes: can be over 1 m deep in soil forming dense mats
Fruits: elliptical in various shades of light brown, grey and purple
C. dactylon has a membraneous ligule where the leaf blade joins the sheath
Direct Control: Use a forked hoe to remove rhizomes.
Ensure removal is thorough to prevent resprouting
Till land to expose and dessicate rhizomes, but be aware that this action may also spread fragments which can grow new plants
Linum usitatissimum as cover crops to suppress weed
